acceptance_criteria.statement: When the service is down or degraded in the way that caused the previous two incidents, a signal observable by the team's own monitoring is emitted, without a customer report being the trigger.
The signal in AC1 is observable from outside the service (e.g. queryable from its externally exposed operational surface) rather than only visible in logs read after the fact.

When a dependency the service relies on is unhealthy, the service continues to answer requests it can still serve and does not amplify the dependency's failure — demonstrable by exercising the service with that dependency made unhealthy.
A signed-in customer can retrieve aggregate click analytics covering their links collectively in one request, rather than having to read one link at a time.
The aggregate analytics response can be broken down by where the clicks came from, as that phrase was given by the requesting account.
Analytics responses are scoped to the requesting customer: a customer's aggregate figures include only their own links and reveal nothing about another customer's links.
The new analytics capability is reachable over the existing HTTP API surface with no user interface shipped.
Existing behaviour continues to hold after the change: redirects, exact per-link click counts, and the existing documented error contract are unchanged.

constraints: Java 21 and Spring Boot (existing service codebase)
PostgreSQL and Redis only — no new database technology

Brownfield: an existing, documented service with a frozen OpenAPI contract, per-link click counts, soft-deleted links, Redis-backed click deltas flushed to PostgreSQL, and Actuator health/metrics endpoints already present
Stated as the current priority, immediately after the sign-up work
'We would like it soon' — a stated urgency with no date attached
Reliability is stated as the first of the two asks ('Reliability first')
output.goal: Make the existing URL shortener more reliable — so that the team learns of an outage from its own monitoring before a customer reports it, and the service copes better when its surrounding dependencies are unhealthy — and give customers analytics that show how their links are performing overall rather than one link at a time.
in_scope: Reliability of the existing service, treated as the first priority of the two asks
Detection of the service being down or degraded by the team's own monitoring, ahead of a customer noticing (the requirement states the outcome, not the mechanism)

Improved behaviour of the service when things around it are unhealthy, so that an upstream/downstream problem is not made worse by this service (the last outage started elsewhere and this service worsened it)
Analytics that let a customer understand how their links are performing overall, across links, rather than the existing per-link numbers
A breakdown of clicks by 'where the clicks came from', as asked for by one larger account (the phrase is recorded as given and not resolved to a particular dimension)
Work delivered on the existing stack: Java 21 / Spring Boot service with PostgreSQL and Redis
non_functional: Availability: the service must not fall over undetected; prior incidents were detected by customers, which is stated as unacceptable
Observability: failures must be detectable by the operators' own monitoring, ahead of customer reports
Resilience: degradation in surrounding/dependent systems must not be amplified by this service
Operability: the reliability work must be exercisable/verifiable by operators, since its value is only realised during an incident
Multi-tenant data confidentiality for analytics, implied by the domain: aggregate figures are per-customer and must not leak across accounts
Performance: aggregate analytics must not degrade the click/redirect path, which is the service's hot path
out_of_scope: Any user interface for the analytics or for monitoring — the requirement explicitly says no UI in this build
Any new database or storage technology
Choosing or building a specific alerting/paging/on-call product or channel — the requirement asks only that the team knows before customers do
Changes to authentication, authorisation or account management; the requirement says nothing about them
Changes to the existing per-link click count semantics, the click/redirect contract, or existing endpoints beyond what the two asks require
Retention, export, or deletion policy for analytics data — not mentioned
Billing, quotas, or pricing tied to analytics — not mentioned
Analytics for anonymously created links, which today have no owner and no readable click count — the requirement does not address them
SLA or uptime targets expressed as numbers — none were stated
Backfill or reconstruction of historical analytics from before this change — not mentioned
The sign-up work, which is stated as already done and preceding this

answers.Q1: The clicker's country. Derive it from the client IP against a local geolocation database bundled with the service; store the ISO country code only and never the address. We accept the new dependency, the database refresh problem, and the privacy and retention work that comes with it. Referrer is explicitly not what was asked for.
answers.Q2: Both incidents were the same shape and neither involved the health probes. A downstream slowed down -- the database the first time, Redis the second -- and our own unbounded retries against it exhausted the request threads, so a slow dependency became a total outage. 'We made it worse' means our retries. Fix it with timeouts and a circuit breaker on the calls that cross a boundary, with a bounded retry policy and a fallback. Do not change /actuator/health: the platform does not route on it, and the probes were not implicated.

payload.note: Answer set B, the opposite reading of the same requirement on both blocking questions. Reliability is a resilience library -- timeouts, circuit breaker, bounded retry, fallback -- and explicitly not probe surgery. Analytics is a country breakdown from IP geolocation, which brings a bundled database, a refresh story and a retention decision that a referrer rollup would not have needed. Advisory answers accepted as proposed except Q3: leave the health endpoints alone.

output.blast_radius: The worst plausible failure lands on the redirect path, which is the only thing in this service that must never fail and the only thing every end user touches. Source capture is a new write executed inside RedirectController.follow() for every click; that method wraps its whole body in catch(RuntimeException) and answers 404, so a bug in the new code does not produce a 5xx anyone would page on — it produces a correct-looking not-found for a live link, with no-store headers, indistinguishable on the wire from a code that was never issued. Nobody's monitoring would see it, because the failure the existing tests and the existing runbook look for is a 5xx or a hang. The second-worst is quieter still: any change to the clicks:pending hash or its Lua drain breaks the durable-total-plus-pending invariant, and because every instance runs the flush non-exclusively, a mixed-version fleet during a rolling deploy is precisely the condition that breaks it — clicks are double-counted or lost, and click_count is the number this product reports to customers and the one AC8 freezes. Third, adding a fourth Redis round trip per click under a 1s timeout turns a slow Redis into held servlet threads, which is the exact amplification AC3 asks to stop, delivered by the analytics half of the same change. The blast radius of the analytics endpoint itself is narrow by comparison — it is a new authenticated read behind an already-correct prefix filter, and the main exposure is an unindexed customer-wide aggregate over links, plus tenant leakage if it is scoped by post-filtering instead of by owner equality in the query. Detection today would be: a customer reporting dead links, or a customer reporting a wrong count — which is exactly the failure mode the requirement was written to eliminate. This change deserves close review of the click path and the flush loop specifically, and much less of the new endpoint.

breaking_changes.detail: If source counters are folded into the existing pending hash, or the field format or drain script changes shape, old and new pods cannot share the key during a rolling deploy. An old pod's readPending parses fields it does not recognise (it logs 'Ignored N click delta(s) whose key was not a link id' and drops them) while a new pod settles fields an old pod already wrote — the durable-total-plus-pending invariant breaks in both directions, and the overcount branch is the one a customer sees. This is the one change here where old and new genuinely cannot run at the same time.
breaking_changes.mitigation: Do not touch clicks:pending or read_click_deltas.lua. Put source counters in a separate, differently-prefixed key with its own drain script, so an old pod never reads them and a new pod's click-count path is byte-identical to today's. If the pending hash must change, do it as two deploys: deploy N writes both formats and reads both, deploy N+1 drops the old — with DurabilityAcrossRestartTest run against a mixed-version pair, not a single instance.

breaking_changes.detail: RUNBOOK.md documents the aggregate as DOWN when Redis is unreachable while redirects still work. Q3 proposes narrowing readiness to PostgreSQL. During a rolling deploy, with Redis unhealthy, old pods report DOWN and new pods report UP on the same URL — a probe removes exactly half the fleet, all of which can still serve every redirect. AC8 also states existing behaviour is unchanged, and this is existing behaviour someone's deployment config depends on.
breaking_changes.mitigation: Leave /actuator/health's aggregate semantics exactly as documented. Express the degraded-but-serving state as a new Micrometer gauge on /actuator/prometheus (already exposed, no config change) and as an alert expression in the runbook. If readiness scoping is still wanted, it requires editing management.endpoint.health.group in application.yml — a protected path — and must be sequenced as: change the deployment's probe to /actuator/health/readiness first, confirm it, then change the group. It is not a same-deploy change.
breaking_changes.surface: GET /actuator/health (and any Kubernetes probe or operator alert pointed at it)

breaking_changes.detail: Adding a parameter or a method breaks compilation for RedisClickCounter, RedirectController and LinkService simultaneously. Grep confirms those are the only three touch points and that no test double implements it, so the break is compile-time and total rather than partial and silent.
breaking_changes.mitigation: Add a default method or a separate overload rather than changing record(UUID)'s signature, so LinkService's call site and the existing exact-count path are provably untouched by the diff a reviewer reads.

breaking_changes.detail: application.yml pins spring.data.redis.timeout and connect-timeout at 1s with a comment stating the click path talks to Redis three times and must keep answering when Redis does not. A second write per click makes it four. Under a slow (not dead) Redis — a pause, a failover, swapping — worst-case redirect latency rises by one full timeout, and servlet threads are held for it. That is the thread-pool exhaustion mechanism A8 exists to prevent, introduced by the analytics half rather than fixed by the reliability half.
breaking_changes.mitigation: Pipeline the two increments into one Redis round trip so the click's Redis call count does not grow, and land A12's reliability work (bounded timeouts, breaker with fallback) before the source-capture write, not after. Assert the ordering with a test that pauses Redis and measures click latency, not just status code — DegradedDependencyTest currently asserts status and carries a 90s class timeout, so a 4x latency regression passes it.
breaking_changes.surface: The click path's 1s Redis command timeout

breaking_changes.detail: Per A6 the rollup starts at deploy while links.click_count is lifetime, so for every existing link the two numbers disagree permanently and the aggregate is the smaller one. A customer comparing the new endpoint against GET /api/v1/links/{code} — which the contract calls 'exact and current' — sees the new endpoint as broken.
breaking_changes.mitigation: Return the coverage start instant as a labelled field in the response and document it in the operation description and in API.md, so the discrepancy is stated by the API rather than discovered. Name the affected population precisely: every link created before the deploy. No backfill is possible — no per-click data was ever stored.
breaking_changes.surface: Aggregate analytics totals vs per-link clickCount

breaking_changes.detail: The gate set-diffs Spring mapping annotations against the contract's paths and fails on a mismatch in either direction. A controller merged without the contract entry fails the run; a contract entry merged without the controller fails it too. The gate is a regex scan, so a path assembled from a constant instead of a literal string reads as unimplemented.
breaking_changes.mitigation: Land the contract entry and the controller in the same change, with the path as a literal string on the method as LinkController already does. Bump info.version to 1.2.0 per A1 and add a 'What changed in 1.2.0' section, matching the precedent 1.1.0 set.

impacted.notes: The hot path. Today it reads only request.getRemoteAddr(); capturing a referrer means reading a header and passing it to ClickCounter.record(). Its catch(RuntimeException) block answers notFound() — so a throw anywhere in new source-capture code turns a live 302 into a 404, silently, which is worse than a 5xx because the click path is asserted never to 5xx (DegradedDependencyTest.theClickPathNeverAnswersWithAServerError) and nothing asserts it never wrongly 404s a live code during a dependency outage.

Two-method interface (record, pendingDelta). Adding a source argument or a second record method is a compile-level change for its one implementation (RedisClickCounter) and its two consumers (RedirectController, LinkService). Verified by grep: no test doubles or second implementation exist, so the change is contained — but the javadoc contract ('must never throw and must never delay the 302') is the thing being extended and must be restated for the new call.

record() is one HINCRBY into a single hash 'clicks:pending'. A source counter adds a second Redis round trip per click inside a 1s command timeout that the runbook already describes as sized for 'up to three' Redis calls per click. The class javadoc names the single hot key as the first thing to change at volume; a second hash keyed (link, day, source) has strictly worse cardinality because the field count is attacker-influenced via the Referer header.

Unchanged if the rollup gets its own script, but its guarantees are load-bearing and easy to break by imitation: non-destructive read, exact-zero HDEL sweep, single-key atomicity so it survives Redis Cluster. A source drain that copies this file and moves rather than copies reintroduces the timeout-loses-clicks failure the file exists to prevent. If instead sources are folded into the existing hash, this script's field format (UUID -> long) changes and mixed-version pods misparse it.

@Scheduled(fixedDelay ${app.click.flush-interval:PT5S}), batch 500, single-threaded, every instance runs it. Draining a second, larger, higher-cardinality rollup in the same loop makes the existing click-count flush wait behind it. A stalled or slow rollup drain therefore degrades links.click_count freshness — which is the number AC8 freezes — with no signal today (the clarification's Q2 third failure mode).

One transaction per link, deliberately a separate bean for the proxy boundary. Rollup writes add PostgreSQL write volume alongside the existing per-link UPDATE links SET click_count = click_count + :delta; contention or a slow rollup upsert extends the transaction window that the existing write-then-settle invariant depends on.

toResponse() computes clickCount as link.getClickCount() + clickCounter.pendingDelta(id), reading durable first and pending second on purpose. Any change to the pending hash shape, to settle(), or to the flush ordering changes this exact number, which AC8 and the contract both pin ('exact and current'). It is also called once per row in list(), so it is already N Redis calls per page.

Needs a new owner-scoped aggregate query. The only existing owner index is ix_links_owner_listing (customer_id, created_at DESC, code ASC), which covers findOwnedBy's exact ordering and does nothing for a join from links to a rollup table. A customer-wide aggregate with no supporting index is a sequential scan proportional to account size on a table that also serves the redirect lookup.

New rollup table keyed (link_id, day_utc, source). PROTECTED PATH (orchestrator/pipelines/sdlc.yaml protected_paths: service/src/main/resources/db/migration/**) — a human is on this diff whatever the node's autonomy. spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto is 'validate', so the entity mapping and the DDL must agree exactly or the service fails to start. V4's note sets the deploy rule: ship the migration ahead of the code that writes to it, not with it.

links gains a child table. Rows are never deleted here ('Nothing is ever deleted', soft delete so codes cannot be reissued), and the requirement puts retention explicitly out of scope, so a per-(link, day, source) table inherits unbounded growth by default. Referer is caller-supplied, so cardinality is attacker-influenced — the clarification's Q6 cap is the only thing bounding it.

The frozen contract, version 1.1.0, 1448 lines, 11 documented operations. The routes_match_openapi gate (orchestrator/sdlc/gates.py:1215) does a set diff of Spring @*Mapping literals against the contract's paths and FAILS on any route present in one and not the other — so the endpoint and the contract entry must land in the same change. A1 makes this an additive 1.2.0 bump.

New authenticated read under /api/v1. Must spell the path out in full on the method (LinkController's stated convention and what the regex-based route gate can parse — the gate cannot resolve constant-valued or composed paths).

Owns MAX_PAGE_SIZE=100 and requireValidPaging(), both private static. A11 requires the new endpoint to reuse the page/size 400 rules — refuse rather than clamp, with fields {size: 'must be between 1 and 100'}. Copying that logic rather than extracting it means two paging contracts that can drift; the contract documents one.

Registered by WebConfig for the servlet pattern /api/v1/* — a prefix mapping, so a nested path such as /api/v1/analytics/... is authenticated automatically, with no code change. The exemption set is exact string equality over three paths; the new route must not be added to it. This is the file where a mistake is invisible: the contract itself warns that no existing test asserts 401 for a token-free request against a newly exempted neighbour.

Closed catalogue; tests assert exact bodies against it. Q7 resolves to adding no entry. Note the constraint this creates: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE's message is literally 'Temporarily unable to accept new links.' and DegradedDependencyTest asserts that exact string, so a 503 on a read would be either a wrong message or a catalogue addition AC8 forbids.

Adding an ANALYTICS bucket is additive to the enum. Worth knowing: RedisTokenBucketRateLimiter fails open when Redis is down (asserted by DegradedDependencyTest.throttlingFailsOpenRatherThanRefusingEveryClick), so a new bucket in front of an expensive PostgreSQL aggregate is unmetered during exactly the outage in which it is most expensive.

A10 routes every new setting here. The class javadoc declares this record part of the frozen contract — the only thing the blind implement and author-tests branches share about configuration — so added components are a contract change, and every one needs a @DefaultValue so a key absent from application.yml degrades rather than failing to bind.

Two findings: (1) management.endpoints.web.exposure.include already lists prometheus, so new Micrometer meters need no config change at all; (2) there is no management.endpoint.health.group.* block, so the readiness scoping in Q3 cannot be done without editing this file — it must be escalated as a protected-path change, not worked around.

PROTECTED PATH. actuator and micrometer-registry-prometheus are already present, so metrics need no new dependency. A8's resilience library (Resilience4j) does need one, and that puts a human on the diff.

Unauthenticated (the session filter is registered for /api/v1/* only). New meters land on a publicly scrapeable surface: tagging by customer id, link id or referrer host would both leak tenant data to anyone who can reach the port and give the registry unbounded cardinality from a caller-supplied header.

Checked and clear: RESERVED_CODES already holds api, actuator, health, metrics and prometheus, so a route under /api/v1 needs no addition and no customer link can shadow the operational surface. Only a new root-level route would require an entry.

Five tests that pause the Redis container and assert the click path still 302s to the right target with no-store headers, never 5xx, never 429s by failure, resumes counting without losing earlier clicks, and that only create is refused (201-or-503 with the exact catalogue message). This is the existing evidence for AC20 and the file A9's new AC3 test must extend rather than replace.

Already provides pauseCounterTier/withCounterTierUnavailable via Docker pause (chosen over stop so the port mapping survives). A9's automated dependency-outage evidence should reuse this rather than add a second outage mechanism.

240 tests, 1056 assertions, 0 disabled. The tests_not_weakened gate holds this as a floor and the coverage_floor gate enforces 70% line coverage from target/site/jacoco/jacoco.csv. New code with thin tests fails the run rather than merely lowering a number.

One hash, all pending deltas, read non-destructively and settled by subtraction. The invariant is 'durable total + pending delta = clicks recorded', preserved whichever half is interrupted, and it is what makes non-exclusive reads from every instance safe. Any second writer or format change to this key breaks the invariant in the direction that reaches a customer.

Written only by ClickFlushWriter, read by LinkService.toResponse (getLink and listLinks) and by the LinkPerformanceTest/ClickCountingTest/DurabilityAcrossRestartTest assertions. The new rollup becomes a second, independently-derived count of the same events, and per A6 it starts at deploy — so it will not reconcile with this column for any existing link, permanently.

Its 'Failure modes, from the outside' table and configuration table are the operator contract and are already specific (e.g. the Redis-outage row). A7 adds alert expressions here, Q3 changes a readiness statement here, and A10's new AppProperties defaults belong in the table that already flags three settings as absent from application.yml.
Nine numbered walkthroughs plus an errors section mirroring the catalogue. A new operation with no entry leaves the guide describing a smaller API than the contract.

regression_surface: A click on a live code while the Redis container is paused: 302, Location byte-identical to the stored longUrl (set verbatim, not via location(URI)), and Cache-Control 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0' — DegradedDependencyTest.clicksAreStillServedWhileTheCountingTierIsUnavailable

No 5xx and no wrong-404 from the click path with the counting tier down, on a live code and on an unknown one, over a run of requests — extend the existing assertion so a live code answering 404 fails, which today it would not distinguish from a legitimate miss

Exact per-link clickCount = links.click_count + the Redis pending delta, read durable-first, including immediately after a flush and immediately after a settle failure (the documented transient overcount that self-corrects on the next pass)

Counting resumes after a Redis outage without losing clicks recorded before it: 3 before, N during (may be lost), exactly 4 more after — DegradedDependencyTest.countingResumesWhenTheTierReturnsWithoutLosingEarlierClicks
Click counts survive a service restart with deltas pending — DurabilityAcrossRestartTest, and it must still pass with the rollup drain sharing the flush schedule

The flush loop advances under a hostile rollup: a rollup write that fails or is slow must not prevent links.click_count from being updated in the same pass (ClickFlushJob's per-entry try/continue is per-link today, not per-concern)
503 service_unavailable is produced by link creation and by no other operation, with the exact message 'Temporarily unable to accept new links.' — the new analytics operation must not emit it

Tenant isolation on the new endpoint: another customer's links contribute nothing to the aggregate and are not distinguishable by their absence; NULL-owner anonymous links appear in nobody's aggregate, including that of whoever created them, enforced by owner equality in the query rather than by a filter
Paging on the new endpoint refuses rather than clamps: page<0 and size outside 1..100 give 400 invalid_request with the fields body listLinks already returns

401 with the single unauthorized body for a token-free, malformed-token, expired-token and foreign-key-signed request to the new /api/v1 path — and the three exempt paths (/api/v1/sessions, /api/v1/customers, /api/v1/public/links) remain exactly three, still matched by exact equality
Unknown JSON property on any new request body is 400, per spring.jackson.deserialization.fail-on-unknown-properties

GET /actuator/health returns a bare {"status":"UP"} to an unauthenticated caller with no details leaked, and its DOWN-on-Redis-outage behaviour matches the runbook table unless a human has approved changing it
New Micrometer meters carry no customer id, link id or raw referrer as a tag — /actuator/prometheus is unauthenticated
Redirect latency, not just status, while Redis is slow rather than dead: the click's Redis round-trip count must not increase
Flyway V5 applies cleanly on a database holding existing links, and the service still starts under ddl-auto: validate with the new entity mapped

Referer handling edge cases at the source-capture boundary: absent, empty, non-URL garbage, an over-long header, and an IDN/punycode host — each must bucket deterministically (direct/unknown) and none may throw into RedirectController's catch block

evidence.claim: The click path makes exactly three Redis calls on a cache hit: one Lua token-bucket EVAL (RedisTokenBucketRateLimiter.consume), one cache read (ResolutionCache.get via the Redis CacheManager), one HINCRBY (RedisClickCounter.record). This matches the '1s timeout, up to three calls' comment and confirms a naive source write makes it four.

evidence.claim: A throw anywhere in new click-path code is invisible: follow() wraps its whole body in catch(RuntimeException) and answers notFound() with no-store headers, so a bug turns a live link into a 404 indistinguishable from an unissued code.

Only RedisClickCounter implements ClickCounter and only RedirectController and LinkService call it; no test double exists (grep over service/src for ClickCounter). A signature change is a compile-time break in exactly three files, not a silent one.
evidence.source: grep of service/src; ClickCounter.java (2 methods), LinkService.java:52/274, RedirectController.java:53/73

evidence.claim: read_click_deltas.lua is single-key and non-destructive by design (HGETALL, copy, HDEL only on exact zero), and settle() subtracts what was written. A second key cannot be added to that script without breaking the single-slot property the file explicitly keeps for Redis Cluster — so a source drain needs its own single-key script, and the two increments can only share one round trip by pipelining, not by one EVAL.

One flush loop exists in the whole service: ClickFlushJob.flush(), @Scheduled(fixedDelayString=${app.click.flush-interval:PT5S}), batch 500, per-entry try/continue, and @EnableScheduling is on UrlShortenerApplication. There is no second scheduler and no lock — every instance runs it.
evidence.source: ClickFlushJob.java:43-56; UrlShortenerApplication.java:21; grep for @Scheduled returns one hit

evidence.claim: The service contains no Micrometer code and no custom HealthIndicator today: grep for MeterRegistry / io.micrometer / HealthIndicator over service/src returns nothing. AC1/AC2 are entirely new surface, not an extension of existing meters.

Micrometer is nevertheless on the compile classpath without any pom change: spring-boot-starter-actuator (compile) → micrometer-jakarta9 (compile) → micrometer-core:1.15.12 (compile). micrometer-registry-prometheus is runtime-scope, which is correct for a registry.

Neither db nor redis is in the readiness group by default, so /actuator/health/readiness is already unaffected by a Redis outage with no config change.

evidence.claim: The aggregate /actuator/health does include a Redis indicator automatically — RedisHealthContributorAutoConfiguration ships in the actuator autoconfigure jar and spring-boot-starter-data-redis is present — so the runbook's 'DOWN when Redis unreachable' row is a Boot default, not something this codebase wrote and could quietly change.

No test in the suite asserts anything about /actuator/** : grep for 'actuator' across service/src/test matches only Fixtures.RESERVED_ALIAS and a CustomAliasTest comment. Both the health behaviour the runbook documents and the prometheus endpoint AC2 depends on are currently unasserted.

Redis eviction and maxmemory behaviour were never examined by any prior review ('Where nobody looked'), and docker-compose.yml defines PostgreSQL only — there is no Redis config in the repository to read a policy from.

No public-suffix / registrable-domain capability exists: service/pom.xml declares no such library, and HostNormalizer does trailing-dot stripping, Locale.ROOT lower-casing, IDN.toASCII, empty-label rejection and numeric-IPv4 canonicalisation — nothing that computes eTLD+1. It is, however, directly reusable for canonicalising a Referer host and never throws (it returns Optional.empty()).

Tenant scoping can be done exactly as AC6/A5 require with the existing mechanism: every owner-scoped query is an equality match on customer_id, and customer_id is nullable since V4, so anonymous links fall out of any aggregate without a filter.

evidence.claim: The only owner index is ix_links_owner_listing (customer_id, created_at DESC, code ASC); links has no other secondary index, and click_count is a plain BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 on the same table the redirect lookup reads.

The paging contract to be reused is private static in LinkController: MAX_PAGE_SIZE=100, page<0 → {"page":"must not be negative"}, size outside 1..100 → {"size":"must be between 1 and 100"}, refused not clamped. Reusing it means extracting it, or the two contracts drift.

options.summary: Source counters in one new single-key Redis hash (e.g. clicks:sources) with composite fields link|day|source, its own copy-then-settle Lua drain modelled on read_click_deltas.lua, and the increment pipelined with the existing HINCRBY so the click's Redis round-trip count stays at three. clicks:pending and read_click_deltas.lua are byte-identical to today, so old and new pods coexist during a rolling deploy.

Fold source counters into the existing clicks:pending hash (composite field format) and extend read_click_deltas.lua. One key, one drain, less new code — but old pods log-and-drop the fields they cannot parse while new pods settle fields old pods wrote, breaking the durable-total-plus-pending invariant in both directions during any rolling deploy.

Write source rows (or upserts) to PostgreSQL synchronously on the click path and skip the Redis buffer entirely. Simplest and always reconciles, but puts a database write in the redirect path, which the stated NFR and the existing counting design both exclude.

Rollup row carries customer_id and day_utc alongside link_id, indexed (customer_id, day_utc, source), so the account-wide aggregate never joins links and never touches the table the redirect lookup uses. Slight denormalisation, safe because link ownership is immutable in this schema.

Store the full normalised Referer host as the source value and fold to a registrable domain only in the response layer if that is later wanted. Keeps the reversible direction and needs no Public Suffix List dependency in the protected pom.xml.

unknowns.current_best_answer: Store and return the full normalised host (lower-cased, trailing dots stripped, IDN→ASCII — i.e. HostNormalizer.normalize applied to URI.getHost() of the Referer), because it is the only choice that needs no new dependency and keeps eTLD+1 derivable later.

It is also one-way in the data: full host can be folded to eTLD+1 later, but a table that stored only eTLD+1 can never be un-folded, and no per-click data is retained to recompute from.

risks: Q1 and Q2 are marked blocking and no human answer is present in the upstream context. The whole plan operates on the clarification's proposed answers: if 'where clicks came from' meant country or device, T9-T16 build the wrong dimension against a table that cannot be re-derived; if either prior incident was something other than the three failure modes T3/T4 detect, AC1 ships a signal that will not fire for the thing that actually happened. T1 records this rather than hiding it, but recording is not settling.

U1 is one-way in the data: T9/T11 store the full normalised host because no Public Suffix List is on the classpath and pom.xml is protected. A later ruling of 'registrable domain' folds forward cheaply; a ruling that only eTLD+1 should ever have been stored cannot be undone, and no per-click data exists to recompute from.

A throw anywhere in T12's new click-path code is invisible: RedirectController wraps its body in catch(RuntimeException) and answers notFound() with no-store headers, so a live link becomes a 404 indistinguishable from an unissued code. Nothing in the current suite distinguishes those, which is why T6 and T12 must assert on a wrong 404 specifically and not only on a 5xx.

Mixed-version rolling deploy is the condition that breaks the durable-total-plus-pending invariant. The plan keeps clicks:pending and read_click_deltas.lua byte-identical (T11 asserts it) precisely because an old pod would drop fields it cannot parse while a new pod settles fields an old pod wrote; the overcount branch is the one a customer sees on the number AC8 freezes.

T12's source increment must be pipelined into the existing round trip. A fourth Redis call under the 1s command timeout raises worst-case redirect latency by a full timeout and holds servlet threads, which is the amplification AC3 exists to stop, delivered by the analytics half. The existing DegradedDependencyTest asserts status codes under a 90s class timeout and would pass a 4x latency regression, hence the separate latency assertion in T5.

Redis maxmemory and maxmemory-policy on the deployed instance are unknown and were never examined by any prior review; there is no Redis service in docker-compose.yml to read a policy from. If any allkeys-* eviction is in force, the new higher-cardinality source structure can evict the pending click-delta hash and silently undercount links.click_count. T11's ceiling and key expiry bound the new structure but cannot bound the consequence of an eviction policy nobody has read.

The source component of the rollup key is caller-supplied via the Referer header, so cardinality is attacker-influenced in both Redis and PostgreSQL. The ceiling is enforced inside the Lua increment in T11; if it is enforced only in the drain or only in the response layer, one forged-header campaign grows the table without bound and retention is explicitly out of scope.

If the edge proxy strips or rewrites Referer, every click buckets as 'direct' and AC5 ships an endpoint that is correct and answers nothing. The proxy's header handling is recorded as never verified, and the service already distrusts that layer for X-Forwarded-For.

V5 sits in a pipeline-protected path and routes the run to human approval; the analytics half of the plan (T9, T13, T14, T15, T16) is blocked behind that approval landing, while the reliability half (T2-T8) is deliberately independent of it, per the stated 'reliability first' ordering.

/actuator/prometheus is unauthenticated and reachable by anyone who can reach the port. A meter tagged with customer id, link id or referrer host leaks tenant data and gives the registry unbounded cardinality from a caller-supplied header; T3 asserts against it, but the prohibition has to hold for every meter added later.

T5's fast-fail gate sits in front of Redis calls, and the existing rate limiter fails open when Redis is down. A new analytics bucket in front of an expensive PostgreSQL aggregate is therefore unmetered during exactly the outage in which the aggregate is most expensive.

docs/TODO.md records an unadjudicated failure in which /actuator/prometheus answered 404 where 200 was expected, and no test in the current 240 asserts anything about /actuator/**. If T2 finds the endpoint absent, the entire A7 reliability deliverable rests on a surface that does not exist, and that discovery must precede T3 rather than follow it.

output.blast_radius: The worst plausible failure lands on the redirect path, which is the only thing here that must never fail and the only thing every end user touches. Both halves of this change push into it: a geolocation lookup and a second Redis write now run inside RedirectController.follow(), a method that wraps its whole body in catch(RuntimeException) and answers 404 — so a bug in the new code does not produce a 5xx anyone pages on, it produces a correct-looking not-found for a live link, with no-store headers, indistinguishable on the wire from a code that was never issued, and invisible to every existing test and every line of the runbook, which look for a 5xx or a hang. The reliability half can produce the same symptom by a different route: a statement timeout on LinkResolver's PostgreSQL read, or a breaker open around it, also surfaces as 404 for links that exist. Second in severity and quieter still: anything that changes the clicks:pending hash or its Lua drain breaks the durable-total-plus-pending invariant, and because every instance runs the flush non-exclusively, a mixed-version fleet during a rolling deploy is exactly the condition that breaks it — click_count is the number this product reports to customers and the one AC8 freezes, and an overcount reaches them within one flush interval. Third, the geolocation dimension can ship entirely wrong rather than broken: behind an edge proxy that does not preserve the source address, every click geolocates to one place, the endpoint looks healthy, and the account that asked for it concludes the product is lying. There is also a new privacy surface — client IPs, which today live only as short-lived Redis rate-limit keys, now enter a lookup path and sit one careless log line away from being retained — and /actuator/prometheus is unauthenticated, so a badly tagged meter publishes customer or link cardinality to anyone who can reach the pod. Detection today for any of these would be a customer reporting dead links or a wrong count, which is precisely the failure mode this requirement exists to eliminate. Review attention belongs on the click path, the flush loop, and the breaker's open-state semantics; the new read endpoint deserves far less.

breaking_changes.detail: If country counters are folded into the existing pending hash or the drain script's field format changes, old and new pods cannot share the key during a rolling deploy: an old pod parses fields it does not recognise and drops them (logging 'Ignored N click delta(s) whose key was not a link id'), while a new pod settles fields an old pod wrote. The durable-total-plus-pending invariant breaks in both directions and the overcount branch is the one a customer reads. This is the one item here where old and new genuinely cannot run at the same time.
breaking_changes.mitigation: Keep click counting byte-identical: put country counters under a separate key namespace (e.g. app.click.key-prefix + 'geo:') with their own script, so an old pod never reads them. If the pending hash must change at all, split it across two deploys — N writes and reads both formats, N+1 drops the old — and run DurabilityAcrossRestartTest and ClickCountingTest against a mixed-version pair, not a single instance.

breaking_changes.detail: Today the degraded contract is precise and tested: clicks still 302 from PostgreSQL, the limiter allows everything, counting resumes the instant Redis returns, and creation 503s. A breaker adds an open state that outlives the dependency's recovery, so during and after an outage a new pod refuses creates (ResolutionCache.invalidateBeforeIssuing) and drops clicks for the cool-down while an old pod on the same fleet succeeds. DegradedDependencyTest.countingResumesWhenTheTierReturnsWithoutLosingEarlierClicks asserts exactly +4 immediately on recovery and is the concrete failure.
breaking_changes.mitigation: Scope the breaker to calls that already have a defined fallback (click counting, cache reads, denylist lookup) and never to a call whose failure semantics are a documented status, unless the open state reproduces that status exactly. Set the half-open probe to fire on the first call after recovery rather than on a fixed cool-down, so recovery stays observable within one request. Update the RUNBOOK failure-mode table in the same change, and re-run DegradedDependencyTest, AnonymousCreateDegradationTest and ClickCountingTest as the acceptance evidence rather than a manual procedure.
breaking_changes.surface: Degraded-mode semantics of the click and create paths (circuit breaker per the Q2 answer)

breaking_changes.detail: Country is derived from request.getRemoteAddr(). Nothing sets server.forward-headers-strategy and X-Forwarded-For is deliberately distrusted (AppProperties.RateLimit javadoc; RUNBOOK:144; API.md:433; recorded again in release.json as an unverified deployment fact). Behind the proxy this service actually runs behind, every click geolocates to the proxy — one country, or 'unknown' for a private range — and the endpoint ships correct and answers nothing. The obvious fix breaks something else: trusting XFF with no trusted-proxy list makes every IP-keyed bucket spoofable, including the click and not-found buckets that defend the redirect path.
breaking_changes.mitigation: Settle it with the platform owner before building the dimension, and name the two acceptable outcomes: (a) the edge preserves the source address (PROXY protocol / L4 passthrough), which fixes the rate-limit buckets at the same time and needs no code change; or (b) server.forward-headers-strategy plus an explicit trusted-proxy list — a protected-path edit to application.yml, escalated, and shipped with the rate-limit consequence stated in the runbook. Do not silently read X-Forwarded-For in the geo path only: that puts a spoofable value into stored data while leaving the buckets on the socket address, and no test would show it.
breaking_changes.surface: Source of the clicker's IP address (getRemoteAddr behind the edge proxy)

breaking_changes.detail: There is no application-level retry anywhere in service/src/main (grep: none), and no Hikari or JPA timeout configuration at all — the defaults (30s connection acquisition, no statement timeout) are what turned a slow database into exhausted request threads. Adding a statement timeout changes existing behaviour on the click path: LinkResolver.resolve() is the transactional read behind a redirect, and a timeout there throws into RedirectController's catch, which answers 404 for a live link rather than a 5xx or a retry. A cold cache plus a slow database then reads as mass link deletion.
breaking_changes.mitigation: Set the timeout from measured click-path p99.9 with headroom, not from a round number, and make the resolver's timeout separate from the write path's. Count timed-out resolutions on a dedicated meter and alert on it, so the 404 that results is visible as degradation rather than as a not-found. The configuration lands in application.yml (protected path) — escalate it as a protected-path change with the numbers attached; do not approximate it in AppProperties where the datasource cannot read it.
breaking_changes.surface: Bounded timeouts on the PostgreSQL boundary

breaking_changes.detail: The human answer to Q2 is explicit: do not change it. But any new @Component implementing HealthIndicator is auto-registered into the aggregate, so dependency-aware health added the obvious way changes what /actuator/health reports, and there is no management.endpoint.health.group block in application.yml to scope it out of.
breaking_changes.mitigation: Express dependency state as Micrometer gauges on /actuator/prometheus (already exposed, no config change) plus alert expressions in the runbook. If an indicator turns out to be unavoidable, it requires an application.yml health-group edit — escalate as a protected-path change with the probe-configuration consequence stated, and sequence the deployment's probe change first.

breaking_changes.detail: Per A6 the rollup starts at deploy while links.click_count is lifetime, so for every link created before the change the two numbers disagree permanently and the aggregate is the smaller one. openapi.yaml:797 tells clients clickCount is 'exact and current', so a customer comparing the two sees the new endpoint as broken.
breaking_changes.mitigation: Return the coverage-start instant as a labelled field in the response body, and state it in the operation description and in docs/API.md — the affected population is precisely every link created before the deploy. No backfill is possible; say so rather than leaving support to discover it.
breaking_changes.surface: Aggregate country totals vs per-link clickCount

breaking_changes.detail: The gate set-diffs Spring mapping annotations against the contract's paths and fails in either direction, by regex over the sources. A controller merged without a contract entry fails the run, a contract entry without a controller fails it too, and a path assembled from a constant rather than a literal reads as unimplemented.
breaking_changes.mitigation: Land the contract entry and the controller in one change, path as a literal string on the method as LinkController already does; bump info.version to 1.2.0 and add a 'What changed in 1.2.0' section, matching the precedent 1.1.0 set.

impacted.notes: The hot path, and now the only source of the clicker's IP: line 64 reads request.getRemoteAddr() (already, for the rate-limit key) and nothing else in the request is trusted. Country capture means a geo lookup inside follow(). Its catch(RuntimeException) at line 86 answers notFound() — so any throw from new lookup or capture code turns a live 302 into a 404 with no-store headers, indistinguishable on the wire from a code never issued, and never a 5xx that DegradedDependencyTest.theClickPathNeverAnswersWithAServerError or any alert would see.

Two methods (record(UUID), pendingDelta(UUID)). Carrying a country to the counter changes record()'s signature or adds an overload. Grep confirms exactly one implementation (RedisClickCounter) and two consumers (RedirectController.follow, LinkService.toResponse) and no test double, so the break is compile-time and total. The javadoc contract 'must never throw and must never delay the 302' is what is being extended.

record() is a single HINCRBY on 'clicks:pending'. A per-(link,day,country) counter is a second Redis round trip per click inside the 1s command timeout that application.yml and RUNBOOK both describe as sized for 'up to three' Redis calls. Country cardinality is bounded (~250) unlike a referrer, but the hot-key problem the class javadoc names first is made worse, not better.

The drain loop is per-link: read (non-destructive) → write durably → settle. If the country rollup is drained in the same pass, a failing rollup write must not stop counter.settle() for click_count, or click deltas are re-added on the next pass and customers see an overcount. Every instance runs this schedule non-exclusively; that is safe today only because of the copy-then-settle invariant.

Exists as a separate bean solely for the @Transactional proxy boundary (one transaction per link). A rollup upsert added to the same transaction couples the click_count increment to the new table's availability; a second bean/transaction keeps them independent but needs the same self-invocation care.

Unchanged if the rollup gets its own script, but its guarantees are load-bearing and easy to break by imitation: copy-never-move, exact-zero HDEL sweep, single-key atomicity for Cluster. A country drain that moves rather than copies reintroduces the timeout-loses-clicks failure the file exists to prevent.

Field format is UUID→long, parsed in RedisClickCounter.readPending with an 'Ignored N click delta(s) whose key was not a link id' fallback. Folding (link,day,country) fields into this hash makes old pods drop them and new pods settle what old pods wrote — the durable-total-plus-pending invariant breaks in both directions during a rolling deploy.
A second Lua script loaded the same way (ClassPathResource + DefaultRedisScript). Must stay single-key and non-destructive for the same reasons documented in read_click_deltas.lua.

PROTECTED PATH (orchestrator/pipelines/sdlc.yaml:55 'service/src/main/resources/db/migration/**') — a human on the diff, whatever the node autonomy. spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate, so the migration must ship ahead of the code or startup fails; V4's header records that ordering rule explicitly. Keyed (link_id, day_utc, country) with its own index; the existing ix_links_owner_listing (customer_id, created_at DESC, code ASC) does not serve this join.

Two numbers now describe clicks: the lifetime durable total (plus pending) that openapi.yaml:797 calls 'exact and current', and a rollup that starts at deploy and is broken down by country. They cannot reconcile for any existing link, and no backfill is possible — no per-click data was ever stored.

New owner-scoped aggregate query. Tenant isolation here is an invariant in the query plan (class javadoc; findOwnedBy's 'where l.customerId = :customerId'), and V4's header explains that SQL equality never matches NULL, which is what keeps anonymous links out. A post-filter or a join that starts from the rollup table instead of from links would lose both properties.

toResponse() reads durable then pending, in that order deliberately, to keep the two-tier count honest (AC8 freezes this). It is also a compile-time consumer of ClickCounter, so an interface signature change lands here even though its behaviour must not move at all.

MAX_PAGE_SIZE=100 and requireValidPaging() are private to this class. A per-link analytics array paged with page/size must repeat the same 400 rules (refuse, never clamp) or the service ships two paging contracts; the duplication is the risk, not the change.

info.version 1.1.0 → 1.2.0 plus one new operation. Two gates bind it: routes_match_openapi (gates.py:1215) set-diffs Spring mapping annotations against the contract's paths and fails in either direction, and contract_frozen hashes the declared contract files at the entry of both parallel branches. Path must be a literal string on the method, as LinkController already writes them.

PROTECTED PATH (sdlc.yaml:54) — writing it forces PENDING_APPROVAL, by design, because a dependency added by an agent is a supply-chain change. Q1 forces a geolocation reader library, and Q2's circuit breaker likely forces a resilience library. Neither is managed by the Spring Boot 3.5.16 BOM, so both need literal pinned versions decided now; the build can reach repo1.maven.org/repo.maven.apache.org only.

New shipped data, accepted explicitly by the human answer to Q1. Consequences the repository does not currently handle: a multi-tens-of-MB binary in a repo with no LFS configuration (.gitignore has no LFS entries), a licence and attribution obligation, and a refresh path — the database goes stale in the jar, and 'refresh' today means a rebuild and redeploy. Country accuracy silently degrades with no signal unless one is added.

Today the clicker's IP is used for one thing and never stored: a Redis rate-limit key ('ratelimit:' prefix, RedisTokenBucketRateLimiter) with a window TTL. It is not logged and not written to PostgreSQL. This change routes it through a geo lookup on every served redirect; Q1 permits storing the ISO code only. The retention/log surface (WARN lines in RedisClickCounter, ERROR in RedirectController) must be checked to ensure no address reaches the log or the rollup.
impacted.path: Client IP → country lookup (new data flow on the click path)

impacted.notes: PROTECTED PATH and A10 says do not edit it — but its current silences become load-bearing here. (1) No server.forward-headers-strategy and no trusted-proxy list, and X-Forwarded-For is deliberately distrusted (AppProperties.RateLimit javadoc, RUNBOOK:144, API.md:433), so getRemoteAddr() behind the edge proxy is the proxy. (2) There is no spring.datasource.hikari or JPA query-timeout block at all, so Q2's 'bounded timeouts' on the PostgreSQL boundary have nowhere to live except this file. (3) management.endpoints.web.exposure already includes prometheus, so new meters need no config change. Any edit is an escalation, not a workaround.

The sanctioned place for new settings (analytics window defaults, rollup retention, breaker thresholds, geo enable/disable). Every key needs a @DefaultValue so a key absent from application.yml degrades here rather than failing to bind, and the names are also the contract the test branch guesses at.

Entirely new surface: grep for MeterRegistry / io.micrometer / HealthIndicator over service/src returns nothing today. Micrometer is already on the compile classpath via spring-boot-starter-actuator, and micrometer-registry-prometheus is runtime-scope, so no pom change is needed for meters alone.

Unauthenticated and outside the session filter (registered for /api/v1/* only; RUNBOOK 'Health and metrics'). Two traps: any new @Component HealthIndicator auto-joins the aggregate and would change /actuator/health, which the human answer to Q2 forbids; and new meter tags are world-readable, so no customer id, link id or IP may appear as a tag — country and link-count tags need a cardinality bound.

The one place a 503 comes from: invalidateBeforeIssuing() throws service_unavailable when the tier is unreachable, and that is what makes creation the thing that degrades. A breaker in front of Redis changes when that fires — an open breaker keeps refusing creates after Redis has recovered, and a breaker that skips evictions on invalidateAfterCommit() puts the published 60-second takedown bound back on TTL alone.

Fails open by design; DegradedDependencyTest asserts zero 429s during a Redis outage. A breaker around the limiter's Redis call must preserve fail-open, and its open state must not become a second, slower way to deny. Adding an analytics bucket also means a new RateLimitBucket enum constant and an AppProperties field.

A PostgreSQL boundary call on the create path with an explicit fail-open policy (app.threat.fail-open=true, logged every time). Adding a timeout or breaker here converts slow-denylist into ThreatVerdict.UNAVAILABLE more often: links get accepted unchecked (fail-open) or every create 503s (fail-closed). Either shift is a security-posture change, not just a latency change.

The filter is registered for the prefix pattern /api/v1/* and the exemption list is exact path equality, so a new operation under /api/v1/** is authenticated with no change here — and one placed anywhere else would be unauthenticated, which is AC6's failure mode. Worth asserting rather than assuming.

The existing AC20/AC3 evidence, and the test most likely to be broken by the breaker. countingResumesWhenTheTierReturnsWithoutLosingEarlierClicks asserts exactly +4 immediately after Redis resumes; a breaker still open through its cool-down loses those clicks and fails it. Its assertions are on status only, with a 90s class timeout, so a large click-latency regression passes it silently.

Every test drives the service over http://localhost:<port>, so getRemoteAddr() is a loopback address with no country. The country dimension cannot be exercised end to end without a seam, and the seam must not be 'trust a header' or the test proves a behaviour the production posture forbids.

Owns the 'Failure modes, from the outside' table (which currently states DOWN-with-Redis, uncounted clicks, fail-open limiting, 503 on create), the timeout note 'the click path talks to Redis up to three times', and the configuration table. Needs the new metrics, the example alert expressions (A7), the geo database refresh procedure, and any change to what degradation looks like.

Numbered walkthrough plus 'Errors', 'Rate limits' and 'Not in this build'. The new operation needs a section, and the coverage-start caveat (A6) belongs here beside the existing 'clickCount is exact and current' claim.

regression_surface: GET /{code} on a live link while Redis is paused: 302, exact Location, Cache-Control no-store (DegradedDependencyTest.clicksAreStillServedWhileTheCountingTierIsUnavailable)

The click path never answers 5xx and never answers 404 for a live code — including while a dependency is slow rather than dead, which no current test covers (DegradedDependencyTest.theClickPathNeverAnswersWithAServerError)

Counting resumes on the exact request after Redis returns: 4 clicks after recovery must read as +4, which a breaker cool-down defeats (DegradedDependencyTest.countingResumesWhenTheTierReturnsWithoutLosingEarlierClicks)
The rate limiter still fails open during a Redis outage: zero 429s on clicks and on unknown codes (DegradedDependencyTest.throttlingFailsOpenRatherThanRefusingEveryClick)

Degradation stays spent on creation: POST /api/v1/links returns 503 service_unavailable with the documented body during a Redis outage while clicks keep serving (DegradedDependencyTest.degradationIsSpentOnAcceptingLinksRatherThanOnServingClicks, AnonymousCreateDegradationTest)

Per-link clickCount stays exact: immediate visibility after one click, correctness under concurrent clicks on one link, independence between links, retention after delete (ClickCountingTest.*, LinkPerformanceTest.anOwnerSeesTheirLinkAndItsClickCount)
Click totals survive a restart with no double count and no loss across a flush boundary (DurabilityAcrossRestartTest)
Click-path latency, not just status, with Redis paused and with Redis slow — the added Redis round trip and the geo lookup are both latency regressions that a status-only assertion passes

Tenant isolation on the new aggregate: another customer's links contribute nothing, and another customer's code is 404 with a byte-identical body (TenantIsolationTest, LinkPerformanceTest.anotherCustomersLinkAndAnUnissuedCodeAnswerIdentically)
Anonymous NULL-owner links appear in nobody's aggregate, including the aggregate of the account that created them (AnonymousLinkInvisibilityTest)
The 60-second takedown bound delivered by active invalidation on delete, expiry change and abuse report — at risk if a breaker skips ResolutionCache evictions (DeleteLinkTest, AbuseReportTest)
Paging rules on the new endpoint match listLinks exactly: page<0 and size outside 1..100 refused with 400 invalid_request and field detail, never clamped
The closed error catalogue: no new code, no 403, no 410, unknown request property still 400 (ApiExceptionHandler, docs/API.md 'Errors')
Application startup after V5 with spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate, and startup on a database where V5 has not yet run
Actuator: /actuator/health still reports exactly what it reports today after the observability work, and /actuator/prometheus exposes no customer id, link id or IP as a tag
Mechanical gates that this change is coupled to: routes_match_openapi (annotations vs contract, both directions), links_resolve over the edited docs, coverage_floor at 70%

options.summary: Depend on org.elasticsearch:geolite2-databases:20191119 from Maven Central. No file to obtain, no human in the fetch path, resolves today. But the data is from November 2019, the artifact has had no release since, the jar is 35 MB and carries City and ASN databases the feature does not use, and 'refresh' has no mechanism at all. CC BY-SA 4.0 attribution obligation applies.

Use com.maxmind.geoip2:geoip2:4.2.1 as the reader and ship a current GeoLite2-Country.mmdb (~9 MB) obtained under a MaxMind licence key by a human and committed under service/src/main/resources/geo with its licence and attribution. Accurate now, Country-only, refresh is a documented human procedure plus a redeploy — which is exactly the refresh problem the Q1 answer already accepted. Costs a person fetching a file and a binary in git history with no LFS.

Same reader, but the database is supplied at runtime from a configured path or mounted volume; when it is absent the service records 'unknown' and reports that state on a meter. Refresh becomes an ops action with no redeploy, and nothing large enters the repository — at the price of the feature being silently inert in any environment where the platform has not mounted the file, and of departing from 'bundled with the service' as the Q1 answer phrased it.

If the proxy terminates the connection, every click geolocates to one country (or to nothing, for a private range), the endpoint looks healthy, no test fails, and the account that asked for analytics is shown a number that is simply false. It is also unrecoverable after the fact: no per-click data is stored, so a wrong dimension cannot be recomputed. release.json already carries this as open finding SEC-3 and calls it 'a deployment fact the repository cannot show'.

So the dimension cannot be exercised end to end without a seam, and the only obvious seam — trusting a header — proves a behaviour the production posture forbids and would land in the test branch as a permanent hole. The test branch is blind to implementation, so the seam has to be named in the frozen contract (a property name) or it cannot be written at all.

unknowns.current_best_answer: Recovery visible on the first call: half-open after at most one flush interval (5 s), permitted calls 1. Also keep the breaker off RedisClickCounter.record(), which already cannot throw and is bounded by the 1 s command timeout — the calls that need it are the ones with unbounded waiting behind them.

payload.detail: all 8 acceptance criterion/a covered by the plan

risks: The feasibility verdict is 'blocked' and three unknowns are still open at plan time: U1 (does the edge proxy preserve the clicker's source address), U2 (which country database, from where, at which pinned Maven coordinate) and U5 (is a protected-path application.yml edit approved for the Hikari/JDBC timeouts, and with what numbers). T1 escalates them rather than planning around them; T10-T11 and T14 cannot be built correctly until U1 and U2 are answered, and T5's pool-level half cannot be built at all until U5 is.

U1 is one-way in the stored data. Country comes from request.getRemoteAddr(), X-Forwarded-For is deliberately distrusted, and nothing sets server.forward-headers-strategy. If the edge terminates L7, every click geolocates to one bucket, every test still passes, the endpoint looks healthy and the account that asked for analytics is shown a false number that can never be recomputed - no per-click data is stored. The tempting fix (read XFF in the geo path only) makes every IP-keyed rate-limit bucket spoofable, so it is forbidden in T14's deliverables.

A circuit breaker's open state outlives the dependency's recovery, and the current degraded contract is instant recovery: DegradedDependencyTest.countingResumesWhenTheTierReturnsWithoutLosingEarlierClicks asserts exactly +4 on the request after Redis returns, and AnonymousCreateDegradationTest pins the 503-on-create behaviour. T6 must use a first-call half-open probe, never a fixed cool-down, and must not wrap ResolutionCache.invalidateBeforeIssuing in a way that changes when the documented 503 fires or skips invalidateAfterCommit evictions (which would put the published 60-second takedown bound back on TTL alone).

A statement timeout on LinkResolver's read surfaces through RedirectController's catch(RuntimeException) as a 404 with no-store headers for a live link - indistinguishable on the wire from an unissued code, invisible to every existing test and to every alert in the runbook, which look for a 5xx or a hang. A cold cache plus a slow database then reads as mass link deletion. T5 must derive the number from measured click-path latency, meter the timed-out case separately, and T7 must fail on a wrong 404 specifically and not only on a 5xx.

Any throw from the new geo lookup or geo counter inside RedirectController.follow() produces the same silent wrong-404. The geo reader is memory-mapped I/O and the counter is a network call; both are in the blast radius of the one method in this service that converts exceptions into a plausible-looking success-shaped response.

Mixed-version rolling deploy is the condition that breaks the durable-total-plus-pending invariant. If country counters share clicks:pending or change the drain script's field format, an old pod drops fields it cannot parse while a new pod settles fields an old pod wrote, and the overcount branch reaches customers on links.click_count - the number AC8 freezes - within one flush interval. T13 keeps clicks:pending and read_click_deltas.lua byte-identical and asserts it by reading the file.

The click path makes three Redis calls today under a 1s command timeout, and both application.yml and the runbook are sized for that. A fourth call for the country counter raises worst-case redirect latency by a full timeout while Redis is paused and holds servlet threads - the exact amplification AC3 exists to stop, delivered by the analytics half. DegradedDependencyTest asserts status only under a 90s class timeout and would pass a 4x latency regression, so T14 needs its own latency and round-trip-count assertion.

Three protected paths are on the critical path and each routes the run to human approval: service/pom.xml (geoip2 and resilience4j coordinates, neither managed by the Boot 3.5.16 BOM, both needing literal pins that must be right once), service/src/main/resources/db/migration/V5__*.sql, and service/src/main/resources/application.yml if U5 is approved. The build can reach only repo1.maven.org and repo.maven.apache.org, so the geo database file cannot be fetched at build time - it arrives as a committed binary in a repository with no Git LFS, or the feature is inert.

The bundled country database goes stale in the jar with no signal: refresh means a human fetch, a commit and a redeploy. Accuracy degrades silently unless a build-date gauge and a runbook procedure exist (T11, T20).

The clicker's IP is today used for exactly one thing and never stored - a short-lived Redis rate-limit key. This change routes it through a lookup on every served redirect. One careless log line or one exception message carrying the address turns a bounded ephemeral use into retained personal data, in a codebase that already logs WARN from RedisClickCounter and ERROR from RedirectController.

/actuator/prometheus is unauthenticated. A meter tagged with customer id, link id or IP leaks tenant data to anyone who can reach the pod; a country tag is bounded at ~250 but only if 'unknown' is a single bucket and unmapped inputs cannot mint new tag values.

Per A6 the rollup starts at deploy while links.click_count is lifetime, and openapi.yaml:797 tells clients clickCount is 'exact and current'. For every link created before the change the two numbers disagree permanently and the aggregate is the smaller one; if the coverage-start instant is not in the response body and in both docs, the first customer comparison reads as a bug.

Retention for the per-(link, day, country) rollup is unset (U6) and is far cheaper to choose before the table exists than to shorten after customers can see history. T12 must land the retention decision in the migration and T21 in a pruning job, or the commitment defaults to forever by accident.
